dataset_name: SIH 2026 Industrial Energy Transition Optimizer Case Study Library
description: Benchmark factory cases for testing the Industrial Energy Transition Optimizer. data_quality_policy.source_backed: Directly supported by an uploaded source or existing project knowledge base.
data_quality_policy.benchmark_assumption: Synthetic factory-level value created for optimizer testing and not a measured factory value.
data_quality_policy.inference: Engineering inference based on documented process characteristics.
data_quality_policy.rule: The application must not display benchmark assumptions as measured factory data.

provenance_notes.food_processing: Existing project food-processing knowledge base explicitly treats the sector as heterogeneous and recommends technology matching by product, temperature, steam, refrigeration, drying, scale and operating profile.
provenance_notes.biomass: The MNRE-GIZ biomass report identifies textiles and food processing among sectors where biomass-based green heat and steam can be deployed and emphasizes biomass supply-chain reliability and multi-fuel boiler configurations.
provenance_notes.electrification: The electrification report provides the complementary case that renewable-powered industrial heat technologies can be economically competitive, particularly at lower temperatures and where onsite/captive renewable electricity can reduce electricity cost.
provenance_notes.mcda: FlexiHeat-DST supports transparent multi-criteria technology selection and scenario analysis rather than relying on a single metric.
provenance_notes.factory_values: All factory-level energy consumption, costs, budgets, capacities and resource scores in this Part 1 dataset are benchmark assumptions intended for software testing unless explicitly labelled otherwise.

merge_metadata.factory_level_values: benchmark_assumptions unless explicitly identified as source-backed
merge_metadata.note: Parts use different case schemas; this merge preserves each case object exactly rather than silently reshaping fields. Consumers should use case-specific adapters or a versioned union schema.
